30111.notes: Montana tax-lien assignment county (no competitive premium auction). Yellowstone County Treasurer attaches tax liens on the first working day of August; investors purchase assignments by mailing owners a Notice of Pending Assignment (certified mail, postmarked Aug 15 for the lottery cycle), then submitting mailing proofs, a preference-ordered Excel list, and $50 per-assignment fee by noon Aug 28. Assignments are awarded Aug 29 via county lottery (snake-method randomizer), not high bid. After Aug 29 remaining liens are first-come/first-served with 14–60 day notice. Subsequent taxes may be paid onto existing assignments June 1–July 30. Final-year process: owner-occupied residential dwellings go to public auction; other parcels issue tax deed to lienholder after statutory notice (MCA Title 15 Ch. 17–18). County recommends quiet title after tax deed.
30111.auctionFormat: Assignment lottery / first-come (not competitive premium bid); later tax-deed auction for some residential parcels

auctionPlatform.label: Yellowstone County Treasurer — Tax Liens / Assignments

30111.auctionFrequency: Annual assignment cycle (Aug attach → Aug 15 notice → Aug 29 lottery); post-lottery first-come remaining; tax-deed auctions only when lienholder applies in final redemption year
30111.depositRules: No bid premium deposit. Pay full delinquent amount + $50 assignment fee per parcel (cash, check, money order, or cashier’s check). Lottery attendance optional if payment pre-delivered by Aug 28 noon. Auction-property winners who are not the lienholder post 5% of bid or $200 (whichever greater) at sale; full payment by cash/cashier’s check within 24 hours. Tax deed fee $25 + Clerk & Recorder recording fees when deed issues.

clerkOfCourt.label: Yellowstone County Clerk & Recorder (records tax deeds / proof of notice)

propertyAppraiser.label: Yellowstone County Treasurer / Assessor (combined office functions)

30111.survivingLiens: Assignment is a lien, not title, until tax deed or auction deed issues. After tax deed, most junior private liens are cut off subject to Montana statute and federal tax liens (IRS rights). Owner-occupied residential auction parcels follow MCA 15-18-219 et seq. with statutory opening bid including half assessed/appraised value. Always run full title and litigation guarantee before deed application.
30111.quietTitle: County explicitly recommends quiet title after tax deed issues. Practically required for marketable/insurable title in Montana tax-deed practice.

42075.notes: Pennsylvania RETSL via Lebanon County Tax Claim Bureau. Delinquent taxes turn over in January; ~17 months later Notice of Sale; Upset Tax Sale held second Monday of September at 5:00 p.m. in the auditorium of the Lebanon County Municipal Building, 400 South 8th Street. Upset buyers assume judgments, liens, and mortgages. Unsold parcels get 60-year title search, court petition, then Judicial Sale free and clear of taxes/mortgages/liens/judgments after proper notice (post-search liens can still attach). Online pre-registration required ($25 non-refundable per bidder) even though bidding is in person.

auctionPlatform.label: Lebanon County Tax Claim Bureau — Upset / Judicial Sale

42075.auctionFrequency: Upset annually second Monday of September at 5:00 p.m.; Judicial after court approval of unsolds
42075.depositRules: Mandatory pre-registration ($25 non-refundable). Bidder affidavit/application (individual or business) required. Payment and certified-funds rules in Conditions of Sale — obtain copies before sale day. Act 33 / RETSL bidder certification compliance required.
